svg.title: Thirty Days to a Tested Retail Operating System
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-operating-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to a Tested Retail Operating System; subtitle: Prepare evidence, integrations, and economics before increasing exposure.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Four milestones cover Days 1–30; numeric values are ending days. The canonical time to first deal is 2–6 months, so this sprint establishes readiness rather than assuming revenue within its first thirty days.; caption: Advance with recorded test results and bounded purchasing. Unresolved supplier, product-safety, inventory, or margin issues remain explicit blockers for the affected products or workflows.; stages: label: Days 1–7: establish sourcing and unit economics; value: Week 1 ends with a documented product shortlist; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Obtain dealer terms, sample invoices, applicable safety records, and 3PL quotes. Build SKU contribution sheets that include duties, shipping, payment costs, returns, and explicit acquisition assumptions.; label: Days 8–14: connect inventory and order routing; value: Week 2 ends with repeatable integration test evidence; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Configure Shopify and the chosen 3PL integration. Test duplicate webhooks, stale inventory, partial shipments, payment failures, and address exceptions using test orders without uncontrolled customer charges.; label: Days 15–21: exercise returns and retention workflows; value: Week 3 ends with reconciled customer-lifecycle tests; numeric value: 21.0; detail: Run return, inspection, refund, delayed-shipment, and email opt-out cases. Verify accounting entries and suppression behavior; confirm unavailable products cannot trigger purchase-focused replenishment messages.; label: Days 22–30: validate readiness and constrain exposure; value: Week 4 ends with a funded operating plan; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Review supplier evidence, test results, cash runway, and contribution assumptions. If sourcing and readiness are complete, authorize a bounded pilot; otherwise schedule remediation within the 2–6 month first-deal horizon.

Test duplicate webhooks, stale inventory, partial shipments, payment failures, and address exceptions using test orders without uncontrolled customer charges.
